title: "Interactive maps with mapgl"

<!-- A pkgdown article (vignettes/articles/, excluded from the package
tarball): the live maps inline maplibre-gl, ~2.8 MB of HTML. -->

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
has_mapgl <- requireNamespace("mapgl", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = has_mapgl)
```

`vignette("maps")` places pic drawings on the Earth and draws them with
`ggplot2`. This article puts them on an interactive
[MapLibre](https://maplibre.org/) map through
[mapgl](https://walker-data.com/mapgl/), styled exactly as on
[rpic.dev's Maps page](https://rpic.dev/docs/maps/): the engine emits the
MapLibre layers that draw a drawing — fills, solid and dashed strokes, dots,
text and shape titles — and every size in them is **true to the ground**.
Zoom in and a label one inch wide keeps covering the same few hundred metres
of the city; a `thick` line stays as wide as the street it was drawn over.

```{r, eval = TRUE, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
if (!has_mapgl) {
  cat("> The maps in this article need the `mapgl` package",
      "(`install.packages(\"mapgl\")`); it was not installed when this",
      "article was built, so the code is shown without its output.\n")
}
```

## One call: `add_rpic()`

The callout from `vignette("maps")`: a dot on Recife's Marco Zero, a box a
few hundred metres north-east of it and an arrow between them, at 400
metres per inch.

```{r callout}
library(rpic)
library(mapgl)

callout <- pic('
geo_lon = -34.8711
geo_lat = -8.0631
geo_scale = 400          # metres per inch

dot at (0, 0) rad 0.04
B: box "Marco Zero" "Recife" wid 1.3 ht 0.5 at (1.4, 0.9) fill 0.95
arrow from B.sw to (0.06, 0.06) thick 1.2
')

maplibre(style = carto_style("positron"), height = 400) |>
  add_rpic(callout, before = "labels", text_scale = 1.5)
```

`add_rpic(map, x)` takes a map from `maplibre()` or `mapboxgl()` and the
drawing — a `pic()` or a string of pic source (passed to `rpic_geojson()`
with any further arguments), an `rpic_geojson()` result or an `rpic_sf()`
data frame — and
adds three things: a GeoJSON source `"pic"` with the drawing, the six layers
of `rpic_maplibre_layers()` and, unless `fit = FALSE`, a `fit_bounds()` on
the drawing. Like mapgl's `add_*()` verbs it takes the map first and
returns it, so mapgl's own functions (controls, other layers, legends) carry
on in the same pipe. (`rpic_mapgl()`, its earlier name, is the same
function.)

Two arguments tune how the drawing sits on the basemap:

* `before = "labels"` puts the drawing's shapes — fills, strokes, dots —
  *under* the basemap's labels: they are inserted at the start of the
  style's trailing label block — before the first layer after its last
  fill or line layer, where the place and street names begin — so they sit
  over the roads and buildings while "Recife" and the street names stay
  readable over the box's fill. (Not before the first `symbol` layer:
  positron draws `waterway_label` early, under its roads and buildings.) The drawing's own labels
  (`pic-text`, `pic-title`) still go on top, so a basemap label never
  covers "Marco Zero". The style is read to find that layer: here
  `carto_style("positron")` is a URL, fetched once per R session when the
  first map is built
  (offline, a warning says so and everything goes on top). `before` also
  takes a layer id (`before = "water"`), and `NULL`, the default, adds
  every layer on top — the rule of the engine's JavaScript `attach()`.
* `text_scale = 1.5` draws every label of the drawing half as large again.
  By default text is true to the ground like everything else — an 11 pt
  label covers the ground it would cover on the page at 400 metres per
  inch — which makes it small at city zooms; the scale keeps it ground-true (it still
  grows and shrinks with the map) but bigger. Strokes and dots keep their
  ground sizes. `rpic_maplibre_layers(x, text_scale = 1.5)` gives the same
  layers.

A third, `font`, needs no tuning here: by default (`font = "style"`) the
drawing's labels use the basemap's own font — positron's Montserrat — so
a label placed `above` a line sits above it; with the glyph server's Noto
Sans (`font = "spec"`, the engine's choice) its different vertical metrics
put "2 km" on the line.

## What the helper does: `rpic_sf()` and `rpic_maplibre_layers()`

The arrow between Recife and Olinda — two places the source uses but does
not define, supplied as `features` — and a geodesic 2 km circle around
Recife, now at one kilometre per inch:

```{r layers}
two_cities <- pic('
geo_lon = -34.8711
geo_lat = -8.0631
geo_scale = 1000         # one inch is one kilometre

C: circle rad 2 at (0, 0) dashed fill 0.97
dot at C.c rad 0.04
line from C.c to C.e thin
"2 km" above at 0.5 <C.c, C.e>
arrow from C.c to Olinda thick 1.5 color "firebrick"
dot at Olinda rad 0.04
"Olinda" above at Olinda + (0, 0.08)
')
x <- two_cities |> rpic_sf(features = list(Olinda = c(-34.8553, -8.0089)))

layers <- x |> rpic_maplibre_layers(text_scale = 2)
vapply(layers, \(l) l$id, "")
layers[[2]]$paint$`line-width`[1:3]
```

Each layer is a MapLibre style-spec object as an R list — `id`, `type`,
`source`, `filter`, `paint` and sometimes `layout` — whose expressions read
the feature properties under their GeoJSON names (`stroke-width`,
`geopic:kind`, ...). Sizes are true to the ground: a label that is 11 pt on
the drawing becomes 11 pt × `geo_scale` metres on the map, so at one
kilometre per inch it looks small until you zoom in. `text_scale = 2`
doubles every label without touching the strokes.

The map itself is the one call; the layers above are what `add_rpic()` adds
for you, and `before = "labels"` slides the shapes under the basemap's
place names:

```{r manual}
maplibre(style = carto_style("positron"), height = 400) |>
  add_rpic(x, before = "labels", text_scale = 2)
```

Why `add_rpic()` and not `add_source()` + `add_layer()` by hand? The layer
expressions read the engine's property names, so the source must be the
engine's own GeoJSON text (kept by `rpic_sf()` in its `"geojson"`
attribute), not the data frame: `mapgl::add_source()` would re-serialise
the `sf` with its R column names (`geopic_kind`), absent values as `null`
and rounded coordinates. `add_rpic()` hands the text to the widget verbatim
and adds the six layers in order (the four geometry layers before the
style's trailing label block when `before = "labels"`, the two text layers on
top). The layers depend only on the collection's registration (its metres
per inch and latitude) and the font sizes it uses, so other mapgl layers —
choropleths, popups, a basemap of your own — can sit under or over them.

The sizing formulas and the layer table are in the engine's
[docs/geopic.md § 6](https://github.com/milkway/rpic-lang/blob/main/docs/geopic.md#6-rendering-on-maplibre).
